biological_interpretation: Partial NatB and NatA disruption have separable neuronal consequences, so loss of one N-terminal acetyltransferase subunit cannot be inferred from the other; recurrent downstream modules are better engagement readouts than Naa20 transcript abundance.
caveats: The Naa20 target transcript itself was never FDR-depleted, and the assay lacks acetylome or NAA protein measurements.
The Naa10 contrast is an under-engaged null, not proof that NAA10 loss is biologically silent.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
exact_observed_result: Naa20 perturbation lowered a recurrent Snhg11/Kifc2/Repin1/Atp11b branch across thalamic, midbrain and selected GABAergic neurons without FDR-significant Naa20 mRNA depletion. Naa15 produced a different posterior NatA state with Ldhd, Actr1b, Matk, Ring1 and Idh3g induction and Rtn3/Thy1/Atp1b1 repression, while Naa10 remained under-engaged and did not phenocopy either program.
